text: ALL ignores every filter — even ones a user chose on purpose. That's a problem for one very common report pattern.

Picture a table broken out by Category and Year, filtered to Europe by a report-level filter. ALLSELECTED keeps that Europe filter — because the user chose it — but ignores only the Category and Year breakdown the visual itself created.

ALL throws away the Europe filter too, giving you the entire dataset's grand total. ALLSELECTED gives you the total for everything the user actually selected — a true visual total. Same shape, different question answered.

Respect the user's selections, ignore only the visual's own breakdown — that's ALLSELECTED. Ignore everything — that's ALL. Next, the final lesson of the chapter: variables and the habits that keep formulas readable.
